memory_update.text: High-confidence direct node candidates for ai_accelerators_hbm_advanced_packaging: NVDA, TSM, MU, AMKR, KLAC.

The node should be tracked as a linked capacity chain: accelerator demand pulls advanced-node foundry wafers, HBM supply, 2.5D/3D advanced packaging, OSAT/test capacity, and inspection/metrology intensity.

This pass did not include non-US-listed HBM leaders SK hynix and Samsung, substrate/interposer suppliers, or smaller packaging-equipment suppliers; these require a separate global/OTC and sub-USD-1B exception pass.

Potential additional US-listed candidates for later passes: AMD and Broadcom as accelerator/custom ASIC demand platforms; AMAT, LRCX and ONTO as additional equipment/metrology exposures; ASX or other OSAT/packaging names if US listing and liquidity constraints are acceptable.
Add AMKR as a direct US-listed OSAT/advanced-packaging capacity candidate for AI accelerator/HBM integration; prioritize proof of named AI/HPC customers and advanced-products revenue mix.
Add ONTO as an HBM and AI-packaging inspection/metrology candidate with explicit reported demand for Dragonfly inspection and 3D bump metrology.
Add FORM as a probe-card/test-interface supplier tied to HBM and known-good-die/package test complexity; monitor South Korea memory exposure and export-control risk.
Add TER as a major automated-test-equipment supplier with AI semiconductor test and HBM/DRAM final-test exposure.

Future Layer 1B passes should separately scan non-US or ADR suppliers that may be closer to ABF substrates, interposers, HBM suppliers, and CoWoS equipment, including Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, ASE, SK hynix, Samsung Electronics, Disco, Advantest, Tokyo Electron, Besi, ASM International, and Lasertec where investability permits.
Add AMKR as a direct US-listed OSAT/advanced-packaging candidate for the AI accelerator/HBM/2.5D packaging node; monitor advanced packaging utilization and Arizona capacity ramp evidence.
Add ONTO as an inspection/metrology candidate tied to HBM and chiplet packaging yield; strongest evidence needed is production-scale HBM/advanced-packaging orders and backlog durability.
Add FORM as an HBM wafer-probe card candidate; customer qualification with all three major HBM manufacturers is a key Serenity-style stickiness signal.
Add TER as an AI compute and HBM/DRAM test-equipment candidate; the research question is whether test intensity and HBM share gains create a structural rather than cyclical revenue driver.
Add ENTG as an adjacent materials/contamination-control candidate for advanced nodes and advanced packaging; relevance is indirect but qualification barriers may be high.

This pass did not include non-US-primary Asian suppliers such as SK hynix, Samsung, ASE, Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, or Disco, even though they may be closer to physical bottlenecks in HBM, substrates, dicing/grinding, and packaging.
Potential US-listed follow-up candidates for a later pass include CAMT, KLIC, MKSI, KLAC, AMAT, LRCX, COHU, and ICHR, but they require tighter evidence mapping to this specific node before inclusion.

node: AI accelerators, HBM, advanced-node foundry, and 2.5D/3D advanced packaging
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct US-listed universe around the AI compute capacity node. The highest-confidence public exposures are accelerator platform owners, advanced-node foundry/CoWoS capacity owners, HBM suppliers, advanced packaging/test providers, and process-control vendors tied to HBM and advanced packaging yield. This pass intentionally limits the list to five high-signal candidates and does not rank them as investments. Expanded the public-market universe around the AI accelerator/HBM/advanced-packaging capacity node by prioritizing US-listed suppliers that sit near qualification-sensitive chokepoints: outsourced advanced packaging/test capacity, HBM/AI package inspection and metrology, probe cards, automated semiconductor test, and high-purity materials/process consumables. These are research candidates only, not recommendations. The strongest near-node candidates in this pass are AMKR, ONTO, FORM, TER, and ENTG; all require follow-up checks on customer concentration, order durability, China/export-control exposure, capex timing, and whether AI/HBM revenue is incremental versus cyclical pull-forward. Expanded the US-listed universe around the AI accelerator/HBM/advanced-packaging node toward second-order suppliers that can benefit if bottlenecks migrate from front-end wafers and accelerator design into OSAT capacity, wafer probing, final test, metrology/inspection, and high-purity materials. The five candidates are not buy/sell recommendations; they are research candidates where the Serenity question is whether customer qualification, process complexity, or booked capacity
